solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clutch twisted, badly iced inside? Hot plate required (12, two words)

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the following letters come out jumbled
inside tells us the jumbled letters sit within the bent word around them

blocks.note: a clutch is the set of eggs laid at one time
twisted means bent out of shape
taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: A cook's mishaps: a twisted clutch of eggs and badly applied icing, then a demand for a hot plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Clutch suggests a car pedal or a grip, but it is a nest of eggs. 'Hot plate' defines a dish served hot, not a cooker ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict is a cooked breakfast dish of poached eggs and hollandaise, so a hot plateful of food.

clue.text: X and what follows Y – a swindle

blocks.note: X is the Greek letter chi
Z comes after Y in the alphabet

explanation.surface: An algebra or alphabet puzzle that turns out to be a con.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like a Roman letter but is read as its Greek name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiz is a Chambers word for a cheat or swindle, as in Molesworth's schoolboy slang.

clue.text: Test in cliff revealing limestone rock (8, two words)

indicators.note: in places the exam word within the word for a rocky face

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a crag is a steep rocky cliff

explanation.surface: A geologist's test on a cliff face reveals a type of limestone.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral rag is a rubbly limestone formed largely from fossil coral, found in southern England.

clue.text: Bird shedding top (i.e. with no hint of chagrin) in Edinburgh joint

indicators.note: shedding its top means the bird's name loses its first letter
a hint of a word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: the chough is a red-legged crow
the bracket confirms the letter shed is the first of chagrin

explanation.surface: A bird losing its crest without embarrassment, ending up in a Scottish pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket checks that the dropped top letter really is C. Edinburgh signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hough is the Scots form of hock, the joint of a leg of meat or an animal's hind leg.

clue.text: Italy's pre-eminent spot for pasta

indicators.note: the pre-eminent part of a word is the one in front, its opening letter

blocks.note: a zit is a pimple or spot

explanation.surface: Praising Italy as the finest place to go for pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The spot comes first in the answer even though Italy is read first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ziti is a tubular pasta, like thick macaroni, popular in southern Italy.

clue.text: Shield protecting centre of pectorals in S. European sport

indicators.note: a shield protecting something wraps around it
the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: a pelta is a small light shield of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: A chest guard worn in some southern European game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is the Basque ball game played against a wall, found in Spain and southern France.

clue.text: Pen rat struggling in snare once

indicators.note: something struggling thrashes about, so its letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A rat caught in a pen, struggling in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic sense, here a noun for a trap or trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Trepan was an old word for a trap or a lure used to ensnare someone, a sense now obsolete.

clue.text: Old copper collection (of pans, say) – it's well worth having

blocks.note: the as was a Roman copper coin
a set of saucepans is a collection

explanation.surface: An antique copper pan collection is valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests the metal of the pans, but here it is an ancient coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable thing, something of benefit to own.

clue.text: What's specially threaded puts sailors on course?

blocks.note: to set is to put or place, here setting a course
the crew are the sailors of a ship

explanation.surface: A captain placing the crew on their course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets crew on course' is what a captain does; the two words run together into a screw name.
explanation.definitionFit: A setscrew is a screw, threaded along its length, used to fix one machine part firmly against another.

clue.text: Verse in church? Appeal for help when penning little one

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, like animals in a pen

blocks.note: tich or titch is a small person

explanation.surface: Someone calls for help while shepherding a small child during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A stichos is a line of verse, and in Orthodox liturgy a psalm verse sung between hymns.

clue.text: Base of heraldic border moved to top for old peer

indicators.note: the base of a down light is its last letter, the one that is moved up
moved to top sends that bottom letter round to the front of the word

blocks.note: an orle is a narrow border inside a heraldic shield

explanation.surface: Heraldry talk: reshuffling a shield's border to suit an old nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the base is the last letter, so it climbs to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Eorl is the Old English form of earl, a nobleman, hence an old peer.

clue.text: Deforestation? Sense steres being chopped with little latitude

indicators.note: chopped up letters are cut about and rearranged, as wood is

blocks.note: taken as written; a stere is a cubic metre of timber
L is the abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: Stacks of felled timber are chopped up, leaving little room for manoeuvre: a forest cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: A stere is a cubic metre, used of firewood. 'Deforestation?' with its question mark defines the state that results rather than the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Deforestation leaves land bare of trees, the condition of having none.

clue.text: Keeper dismissing No. 3 for a duck – Aussie's hard projectile

indicators.note: dismissing the third letter for another swaps one letter out and a new one in

blocks.note: a duck is a nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Cricket: the keeper dismisses the number three batsman for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket scene makes 'Keeper' the wicketkeeper, but it is the goalie. A duck in cricket is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a goolie is a stone or pebble, something hard to throw.

clue.text: Cicero? He comes to prominence after Caesar's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
after says the pronoun and hill are placed behind the letter from Caesar

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, a prominence

explanation.surface: Cicero rose to fame after Caesar died.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: Caesar's last letter leads, then He, then the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetor is a teacher or master of rhetoric, and Cicero is the classic Roman orator.

clue.text: US labourer given guidance, jokingly happy

blocks.note: grunt is American slang for an unskilled worker or foot soldier

explanation.surface: An American worker who has been shown the way is quite content.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruntled is a humorous back-formation from disgruntled, meaning pleased or satisfied.

clue.text: French artist recalled (no date), one of seven historically?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the name runs backwards
no date means the letter for date is dropped

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Recalling an undated French painter who might be one of a famous seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seven Sages were the wise men of ancient Greece, so a sage is one of the seven.

clue.text: Small work reproduced close up

indicators.note: reproduced means made anew, so the letters are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: A miniature artwork reproduced in close-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An opuscle is a minor musical or literary composition, a little opus.

clue.text: Pit prepared in hollows for victims of war?

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are worked into new order
in places the worked letters within the hollows

explanation.surface: Pits dug in the ground for those killed in war.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mass graves; the question mark allows prisoners as victims of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Captives are prisoners taken in war, among those who suffer from it.

clue.text: Posture after imbibing hard liquor initially in Scotch bar, upright

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the posture word takes a letter inside
initially points to the first letter only

blocks.note: stance is a way of standing
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone's posture in a Scottish bar after downing hard liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch bar' is not a pub: it is a Scots word for an upright bar or post.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanchel is a Scots variant of stanchion, an upright supporting post or bar.

clue.text: Eastern mine without alteration leads to catastrophe

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: the part of a play that leads to the catastrophe

blocks.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: An Eastern mine left unaltered heads for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In classical drama the catastrophe is the final turn of the plot, not a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Epitasis is the part of a classical play where the action intensifies before the catastrophe resolves it.

clue.text: I resemble worker ant eager to work alongside queen

indicators.note: to work the letters is to knead them into a new form

explanation.surface: An eager worker ant toiling beside its queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer speaks in the first person, defining itself as an ant that looks like a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An ergataner is a wingless male ant that looks like a worker, from Greek ergates, worker.

clue.text: Comedian introducing bit of grossness grates badly

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters are rearranged
a bit of a word here is just its first letter
introducing means bringing something into the middle

explanation.surface: A comic who adds a little vulgarity grates on the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is a gag writer or teller of jokes, a comedian.

clue.text: Trophies arranged on special Orthodox Church table

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Trophies laid out on a special table in an Orthodox church.
explanation.definitionFit: In Eastern Orthodox churches the prothesis is the side table where the eucharistic elements are prepared.

clue.text: Portentous people having entry in big book of words

indicators.note: having entry in means getting inside something

explanation.surface: Important people get a mention in a great dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Omened means bearing an omen, so full of portent.

clue.text: Very small score with No. 2 changing direction completely?

indicators.note: a compass point turned completely round becomes its opposite point

blocks.note: the second letter of the score word, a compass point

explanation.surface: A tiny score where the runner-up's direction changes.
explanation.walkthrough: W is west; reversing direction completely gives east, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenty is a dialect or childish form of teeny, meaning tiny.

clue.text: I've a tiny waist – see it merge fantastically with intake of very small weight! (8, two words)

indicators.note: an intake brings something inside before the shuffle
fantastically suggests wildly altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: g, gram, is a tiny unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a tiny waist, and wonders at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer speaks in the first person: an hourglass is narrow in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg timer is a small hourglass, pinched at its waist where the sand runs through.

clue.text: Abrupt snob cutting in

indicators.note: cutting means removing the two-letter word that follows

blocks.note: a snob is an old word for a shoemaker, and St Crispin is their patron saint

explanation.surface: A snob cuts into a conversation abruptly.
explanation.walkthrough: Snob is used in its old sense of cobbler, so the shoemakers' patron saint stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp manner of speaking is brisk and curt, so abrupt.

clue.text: Show passion getting in variety of seed potato

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are rearranged
getting in means going inside the jumbled word

blocks.note: ire is passion shown as anger

explanation.surface: A gardener gets passionate about a variety of seed potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seed potato' looks like one phrase, but seed is anagram fodder and potato alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Désirée is a popular red-skinned potato cultivar.

clue.text: Waterway fully feeding West Bank city?

indicators.note: the river feeds wholly into the city's name, filling its interior

explanation.surface: A waterway supplying a city in the West Bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Hebron is the West Bank city; the river sits entirely inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river of north-east Spain, a waterway.

clue.text: Attractive shell the old man found with gold inside

indicators.note: found with something inside means enclosing it
inside confirms the precious metal sits within the father

blocks.note: pa is a father, the old man
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Dad found a pretty shell with gold in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paua is a New Zealand abalone whose iridescent shell is prized for jewellery.

clue.text: Health food with alcoholic additive died away

indicators.note: away means removed, taking the word for died out

explanation.surface: A health food that once had alcohol added has lost its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The blocks read as one surface phrase, but brandied minus died leaves the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran, the husks of cereal grain, is eaten as a fibre-rich health food.

clue.text: Record once achieved by two girls (nothing between them)

blocks.note: Lise, a second girl's name, joined directly to the first with no gap

explanation.surface: A record set by two girls, a dead heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing between them' sounds like a tie, but it means the two names are run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Annalise is an obsolete verb meaning to record in annals, chronicle.

clue.text: Dagger: native American beginning to sharpen end of blade

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the Cree are a First Nations people

explanation.surface: A Native American sharpens the end of a dagger blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Creese is a variant spelling of kris, a Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: What may make hacking suits unusually small?

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor wonders what makes hacking jackets so small.
explanation.walkthrough: A hacking jacket is a riding jacket, but here hacking is coughing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussis is the medical name for a cough, which causes hacking.

clue.text: Something akin to cod, ingredient for ragout or skink

indicators.note: an ingredient is a part already contained in the dish

explanation.surface: A fish to go in a stew or a skink, a Scots soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Skink is a Scots soup, as in Cullen skink.
explanation.definitionFit: The torsk is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Range? First of superior lot probably Aga, versatile

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of each following word
versatile means easily turned about, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Shopping for a cooking range: the best of the bunch is probably a versatile Aga.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a cast-iron kitchen range, which steers the solver to cookers; the range is mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe.
